In 1925, a man sold the Eiffel Tower. Then he came back and tried to sell it again.
Con man Victor Lustig read that the tower was rusting, and costing Paris a fortune.
So he forged government papers, and posed as a top official.
He gathered five scrap metal dealers in a fancy hotel, and told them a secret. The city was going to sell the tower for scrap.
One dealer, Andre Poisson, wanted it badly.
When Poisson got suspicious, Lustig confessed he was a corrupt official, who wanted a bribe.
That made him believable. Poisson paid, and Lustig fled to Austria with a suitcase of cash.
Poisson was too embarrassed to go to the police.
So Lustig came back, and ran the same scam again.
This time a dealer called the police, and Lustig slipped away just in time.
He finally ended up in Alcatraz, for printing fake money.
